Commentary.Commentary: Kane Richardson says it was tough to get a wicket, it was hard as they expected but it is nice to restrict them to 140. States they were advised to stick to their strengths and with long boundaries, it is not easy to find them. Ends by saying they are happy with how they did with the ball and he hopes they do well with the bat.

So a better showing from the Lankans with the bat sees Australia chase a tricky target of 143. Will David Warner once again be the man to take his side home or will Sri Lanka have an answer not just for him but rest of his colleagues as well? Join us after the break to find out but for now, Kane Richardson is giving an interview.

It was another good performance from the Aussie bowlers but it was not as efficient in the death as the previous two games. All three pacers, Starc, Richardson and Cummins got two wickets each but the former was relatively expensive courtesy of his last over. Zamapa did not have a good outing as he went wicketless and gave away 30 from his 4. Agar too went wicketless but was once again economical. Overall a decent performance from the hosts with the ball.

After opting to bat, the Lankan innings once again did not get off to a best of starts losing Dickwella in the very first over. Perera though was in the mood and he started off with a flurry and then did the balancing act in the middle. Scoring Sri Lanka's first individual 50 in the process. His 57 along with Bhanuka Rajapaksa's cameo in the end took Sri Lanka to a fighting total of 142.

Excellent end to the innings. 24 runs off the last two overs has seen  Sri Lanka cross 140 the run-mark. A much, much improved performance from the visitors. They definitely have something to bowl at.

A single to end! Very full and on off, Malinga looks to hit it hard but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It rolls on the leg side for one. 24 from the last two overs. Good finish for Sri Lanka. THEY END WITH 142/6!
Swing and a miss! A dot! Malinga is followed as he makes room. He swings but misses.
Another single! Slower one again, Rajapaksa swings but it hits the body of him and rolls on the off side. A leg bye taken.
Just a single this time! Richardson goes full and on middle, this is hit towards covers for one.
SIX! All the way! What a shot to get off the mark! WOW! Powered! The crowd here is going bonkers! It is short and on middle, Malinga hammers it over the long on fence for a biggie.
Very full and on off, this is hit nicely through covers but just for one.
Kane Richardson to bowl the last over of the innings! Also, Lasith Malinga walks out to bat.

OUT! Bowled! Starc ends his spell with a wicket. Good length ball on top of leg, Jayasuriya looks to play a premeditated ramp shot. He misses, Starc does not. The leg stump goes for a toss. Good over through for Sri Lanka. 14 runs off it. Starc finishes with the figures of 4-0-32-2.
Full on off, Bhanuka strokes it towards mid off for a single.
Excellent running. Good length ball on off, Rajapaksa cuts it through point and runs the first one hard. The then look for two and get it with relative ease.
FOUR! 10 in two and the pressure is on Starc! A real loose delivery from him. It is on the pads, Rajapaksa picks it up and pulls it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
SIX! What a shot! Effortless this. Fuller on the pads, Rajapaksa picks it up with his flick and lofts it over the square leg fence for a maximum. Adam Gilchrist would be proud of that shot.
Full on off and middle, Shehan glances it towards square leg for a single.
Mitchell Starc to bowl out. 3-0-18-1, his figures so far.

Eventually they get two! This is on middle, it is worked with soft hands towards mid on. They take on. The non-striker wants another but is sent back. The fielder picks the ball up and scores a direct hit. The ball deflects away from the fielder backing up and a run is taken.

NOT OUT! The foot is down! Flatter and outside off, Rajapaksa looks to guide it down to third man but misses. Carey takes the bails off and appeals. The umpire takes it upstairs. Replays show that Rajapaksa never lifted his foot.
The square leg umpire has gone up to check for stumping. Rajapaksa looks to be in to the naked eye but the umpire wants to be sure.
On middle, it is worked towards mid-wicket for one. Boundaries once again hard to come by.
Good shot! Jayasuriya comes down the track and hits it hard down to long off. The fielder runs to his left, slides and pushes it back in. Saves two for his side.
Fumble and a run! This is floated up on off, Rajapaksa pushes it towards cover. The fielder fumbles and a run is taken.
On the pads, Jayasuriya works it through square leg for one.
Adam Zampa is back on. 3-023-0 are his figures so far.
Length ball on off, Bahnuka once again taps it towards point and looks for a single but does not get it yet again.

Oh direct hit and that would have been close. Good length ball around off, Rajapaksa taps it towards backward point and comes out looking for a single. Shehan sends him back. The fielder has a shy at the keeper's end but misses. Luckily Cummins came to cover up otherwise that could have cost extra runs.
Length ball on top of middle, Jayasuriya taps it towards backward point for a single.
Extra bounce! Good length and on off, Jayasuriya looks to guide it down to third man but it hits the higher part of the bat and it rolls towards point. No runs taken.
No hat-trick. Not a good hat-trick ball though. Outside off, Jayasuriya lets it be. Do not see a lot of leaves in the 17th over. SJ just wanted to ensure the hat-trick is not taken maybe.
Sehan Jayasuriya to face the hat-trick ball. Bhanuka Rajapaksa to join him out in the middle.

OUT! Caught! End of Perera's knock and 150 now looks farfetched as there will now be two new batters out in the middle. Cummins strikes on the first ball of his last over and once again the bowling change works. It is short and on middle, skids through. Perera is way too late in the pull. He only manages a top edge towards the cover fielder where Turner takes it. Also, Cummins is on a hat-trick as he took a wicket on the last ball of his last over and the on the first ball this time.
Pat Cummins is back into the attack. 3-0-22-1, his figures so far.

A couple to end but just the six runs from the over. On middle, it is flicked with soft hands through mid-wicket for two. End of Agar for tonight, he does not take a wicket but just goes for 24 in his 4 overs.
Fired on the pads, Jayasuriya works it towards short fine leg for one.
Quicker and on middle, this is flicked through mid-wicket and a single is taken.
Another single as this is worked through mid-wicket for one. Singles won't harm Australia at the moment.
Very full and on the pads, Perera looks to sweep but misses. It hits the pads and rolls on the off side. A leg bye taken. The players make an appeal but not given.
On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for one.
Ashton Agar is back. 3-0-19-0, his figures.
Outside off, this is slapped down towards mid off for one. 6 runs and a wicket for him.

Good shot for three! Shorter and outside off, Perera makes room and slaps it over covers. Starc runs to his left, the ball stops as it reaches the fence. Starc dives and pushes it back in. Saves a run for his side.
Shorter and on the body, it is pulled through square leg for one.
Well bowled! A length ball around off, Jayasuriya looks to pole at it but gets beaten.
Shehan Jayasuriya walks out to bat now.

OUT! There is nothing on Hot Spot but a spike on Snicko and the on-field call stays. Fernando's stay is a short one and the partnership which was looking good comes to an end. The bowling change does the trick for the hosts. It is a short ball and outside off, Oshada plays a nothing shot. He looks to guide it down to third man but only manages a faint edge to the keeper. An appeal and up goes the finger. Oshada reviews. The first replays does not judge anything. Hot Spot also shows nothing but then Snicko shows a spike. Another timely wicket for Australia.
Edged and taken! Another wicket for Australia or is it? Oshada reviews straightaway. So there might not be an edge.
Perera comes down the track and Richardson bangs it short. It is hit down to long on for one.
Kane Richardson is back as well. 2-0-10-1, his numbers so far.

EDGY FOUR! Excellent over for Sri Lanka. They would hope this is the momentum changing over. This is tossed up on off, Fernando looks to go over covers but gets a thick outside edge which goes down to the third man fence.
Tosses it up on middle, this is powered down to long on for one.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
On middle, this is eased down to long on for one.
A couple now and fifty for Perera. 11th in T20Is and also the first Sri Lankan to score a fifty in this series. He gets there by playing this one with soft hand through mid-wicket for two.
FOUR! Reverse sweep and a boundary! Perera gets into position early and then manages to hit it over the point fielder. Two boundaries in the last 7 balls.
Adam Zampa is back on. 2-0-10-0, his figures so far.
In the air... but safe again! Shorter and on middle, Perera looks to cut but can't get on top of the bounce. He still manages to get it over covers for two.

DROPPED! That is a dolly! It just does not get easier than this. Richardson should have gobbled that. It is another full and wide ball outside off, Perera goes after it but ends up hitting it uppishly to point. It is straight to Kane who does not hang on. This could prove costly as Perera can be very dangerous.

FOUR! A welcome boundary there! First boundary after the Powerplay. There is width on offer and Starc pays the price. This is slapped through covers, uppishly but wide of the fielder at covers and into the fence.
One more short one, it gets big on the batter. Oshada nudges it around the corner and gets to the other end. He is off the mark.
On the pads, this is worked through square leg and a single is taken.
Just over! A slower one, Perera is completely deceived. He ends up pushing at it way too early. He gets enough though to clear the man at covers and collects two.
Change in bowling as well. Mitchell Starc is back into the attack. 2-0-9-1, his figures so far.
One Fernando is replaced by another. Oshada is the new man in.

OUT! In the air... taken! Long boundaries here, not easy to clear, you have to get it right off the middle and Fernando does not do so. Ben McDermott takes his third catch and a timely wicket for Australia as the two were just looking to accelerate. This is a back of a length ball, it is angled into the pads of the batter. Fernando looks to whip it over the square leg fence but ends up getting more height than distance. The fielder there settles under it and takes it nicely. Fernando just never got going, he played at a strike rate of around 90 so his wicket could well be a blessing in disguise for the visitors.
A slower short one! Perera pulls it through mid-wicket and takes another single. Sri Lanka are trying a lot but just can't find the fence at the moment.
One more short one, too quick for the batter again. Fernando tries to pull but mistimes it in the mid-wicket region for one.
In the air... safe! Shorter again, this one has more zip on it. Perera looks to pull but then realizes it is a little too quick. It ends up hitting the bat and lobs on the leg side for one.
Mistimed! Shorter in length on middle, Perera makes room and drags it over mid-wicket for two.
Shorter and around off, not a lot of room to work with. Perera cuts it to point.
Pat Cummins is back on. 2-0-17-0, his figures so far!

Misfield! Still no boundary though. Fernando plays an aggressive stroke. He looks to hit it over covers but gets it a little too straight. The fielder at long on overruns it, the ball goes past him, it stops near the ropes though. Two taken.
Perera comes down the track this time but Agar spots it. He shortens his length. Perera looks to sweep it but then it ends up hitting the pad and it lobs on the leg side for one. Leg bye signaled.
Flatter and on middle, Fernando pushes it through covers and takes one. Dealing in singles at the moment are Sri Lanka.
This is on off, Avishka opens the face of the bat and guides it to point.
Shorter and on middle, Perera goes back and pulls it through square leg for one.
Slightly shorter and on off, Fernando pushes it through covers for one.
6 singles off the over. Shorter on off, Fernando punches it towards cover and keeps the strike.
Flights one off, Perera nudges it to point and gets another single.
Darts one fuller outside off, Fernando strokes it towards point and takes the 4th consecutive single off the over.
Flighted on off, Perera pushes it towards cover and rotates the strike.
Uppish but away. Tossed up on middle, Avishka plays it uppishly towards the vacant mid on region and gets a single.
Floated on off, Perera milks it towards long on for one.
A single to end a decent over for Sri Lanka. On middle, KP flicks it towards square leg for one.

Another couple! Slightly shorter and outside off, Perera plays it nice and late, he cuts it through point for two. When boundaries are hard to come by, running between the wickets becomes crucial and the two are doing it nicely.
This is flatter and on the pads, Fernando nudges it on the leg side and takes one.
On middle, Perera once again flicks it through mid-wicket and takes one more.

Good running! Flatter and on middle, there some extra bounce. Perera looks to work it on the leg side but it goes off the higher part of the bat. That works in the favor of the batting side as they take two.
Flatter and on middle, it comes in with the angle. Fernando ends up defending outside the line, the ball goes off the inner half and through square leg for one.
On the pads, AF glances it to mid-wicket and keeps the strike.
Flights one around the pads, Perera flicks it towards mid-wicket for an easy single.
Zampa gives this one nice amount of air time and bowls it slower through the air on off. Avishka squeezes it to cover for a single.
Floated on middle and leg, KP flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run.

Perera brings out the reverse sweep but does not get a proper timing on it. It is on middle and leg, Perera looks to play the reverse hit but it goes towards short third man off the lower half of his bat.
Zampa starts with a leg spinner outside off, Perera cuts it but finds the man at point.
Adam Zampa is on now! Spin from both ends now.
Another one on the pads, Kusal glances it to the on side and keeps the strike. 6 runs off Agar's first.
Floated on middle and leg, Avishka turns it towards square leg for a single.
Short again outside off, Avishka cuts it through point and takes a couple as the fielder cleans it up.
Short outside off, Perera cuts it towards point. The fielder there dives to his right and looks to stop the ball. He cannot stop it cleanly allowing them to take a single.
Darted on the pads, Kusal turns it to square leg.
Agar starts with a flatter delivery outside off, Fernando punches it towards cover for a single.
Ashton Agar is on now!
Sri Lanka are 41 for 2 after the first six.

TOP EDGE AND FOUR! Perera is riding his luck here. Good length ball around off, Perera looks to pull but gets a top edge on it. The ball falls in no man's land at third man and goes away to the fence.
Slower ball. It is bowled at a 118.9kph. Avishka manages to pull it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Fernando defends it back towards the bowler.
On top of the stumps, Avishka keeps it out.
Length ball around off, Avishka punches it through covers for a couple.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, Avishka defends it towards mid on.
Hits the deck hard on top of off, Kusal defends it off the back foot to get through the over. End of a brilliant over from Richardson. Just 3 runs and a wicket off it.
Back of a length on off, Avishka punches it towards cover and gets off the mark with a single.
Avishka Fernando comes out to bat.

OUT! Mendis holes out! Richardson gets his first of the game. The short ball has done the trick here for Australia. Richardson bangs it in short, Mendis stands tall and pulls it towards deep mid-wicket. Ben McDermott is standing well in front of the ropes. He hardly has to move an inch as the ball goes straight to him. He makes no mistake and takes his second catch of the game. The change of ends does the trick for Kane. Mendis who was looking so good out in the middle has to depart.
Brilliant effort from Turner! Good length ball on off, Mendis pulls it to the right of short mid-wicket. Turner dives to his right and puts a brilliant dive to save runs for his side.
Around the pads, Perera turns it towards square leg and takes a single.
Length ball on off, Mendis pushes it to cover and gets to the other end.
Change of ends for Kane Richardson.

TOP EDGE AND SIX! Luck is going Sri Lanka's way and they are off to their best start of the series. Good length ball outside off, Perera looks to pull but gets a thick top edge on it. There is a man at deep third man but all he can do is watch it sail over the ropes.
Length delivery closer to the off pole, Mendis dabs it down to third man and rotates the strike.
Good length ball on off, Kusal Mendis defends it off the back foot.
Back of a length ball around off, Kusal pulls it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Length delivery around off, Mendis runs it down to third man for a run.

Cummins starts with a length delivery around middle and leg, Perera defends it off his back foot to the side of the ptch on the leg side. They look for a quick single and get it as Mendis puts in a dive and crashes onto the stumps at the keeper's end. In the end he is safe that is all that he would care about.
Pat Cummins comes onto bowl now.
Length ball on off, Perera taps it towards cover and keeps the strike.

FOUR LEG BYES!  Another ball around the pads, Perera looks to flick but the ball goes off his thigh pad wide of the diving keeper. Carey has no chance stopping that and the ball goes away to the fence.
On the stumps, KP keeps it out.
Good length ball on middle, Perera defends it back towards the bowler off the upper half of his bat.
WIDE! Starc misses his line and sprays one down the leg side. Wide signalled.
FOUR! Perera is off the mark in style. On the pads, Perera swings his bat and goes fine down the leg side. The ball races away to the fine leg fence for a boundary.

NOT OUT! The Ball Tracker is not available so the umpire stays with the on-field call. Fuller on leg, Mendis looks to play the uppish flick but misses. The ball hits him on the pads and he takes a leg bye as the ball goes towards point. The Australian players are putting in a huge appeal in the meantime but the umpire shakes it away. Finch signals the 'T'. Replay rolls in and Ultra Edge and Hot Spot confirm no involvement of bat. Weirdly the Ball Tracker is not available so the T.V umpire stays with the on-field call. Now, looking at the replays again and again, is Finch lucky that BT was not available? Because it seems like it might be doing too much. Australia do not lose a review because technology could not be used.

Review time! LBW appeal taken upstairs. Mendis is the man in question. To the naked eye, it looks like the ball is going onto miss the leg stump. But let's see what the replays have to say. Replays are inconclusive while there is no inside edge. But hang on...the third umpire is being told that there is no Ball Tracker available!
On off, Mendis pushes it to point and keeps the strike.
Richardson corrects his line and bowls one outside off, Mendis looks to play on the up but misses.

SIX! First one off the day and a very smart shot too this. Length ball on the body, Mendis picks his shot early and goes over fine leg. The man at fine leg is up inside the circle so no risk. He times it well so the ball also clears the rope.
On the pads, Mendis flicks it to the man at mid-wicket.
Play and a miss. Good length ball outside off, Mendis slashes at it but does not connect.
Kane starts with a fuller ball on middle, Kusal pushes it to mid on.
Kusal Perera walks out at number 3. Kane Richardson to partner Starc from the other end.

OUT! Golden duck for Dickwella! Starc strikes on the last ball of his first over.  Fuller on off and middle, Dickwella looks to flick but closes his bat too early. The ball takes the leading edge and goes towards cover. Ben McDermott moves behind and takes a simple catch. Just like the previous two games, Sri Lanka lose their first wicket early.
Good length ball closer to the off pole. Mendis runs it down towards third man for a couple.
Play and a miss! Length ball way outside off, Mendis throws his bat at it but does not connect.
Beauty! Starc comes steaming and hits the deck hard outside off. It looks to be coming in but straightens after pitching. Mendis looks to play it to the off side but misses.
Low full toss outside off, Mendis drives it to Cummins on the bounce at point.
Starc starts with a full inswinging ball on middle and leg. Kusal Mendis flicks it through square leg for a couple to get Sri Lanka underway.

We are all set to begin! The Australian players are out in the middle and are taking their respective positions in the field. New opening pair for Sri Lanka as Niroshan Dickwella and Kusal Mendis stride out to the middle to open the innings. Mitchell Starc is back in the squad and he is straight into the thick of action as he is all set to start the proceedings with the new ball.

AUSTRALIA (Playing XI) - Aaron Finch (C), David Warner, Steven Smith, BEN MCDERMOTT (IN FOR GLENN MAXWELL), Ashton Turner, Alex Carey (WK), Ashton Agar, Mitchell Starc (IN FOR BILLY STANLAKE), Pat Cummins, Kane Richardson and Adam Zampa.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Kusal Perera(wk), Kusal Mendis, Niroshan Dickwella, Oshada Fernando (IN FOR DANUSHKA GUNATHILAKA), Avishka Fernando, Shehan Jayasuriya (IN FOR DASUN SHANAKA), Bhanuka Rajapaksa (IN FOR WANINDU HASARANGA), Lakshan Sandakan, Lasith Malinga(c), Nuwan Pradeep and Lahiru Kumara (IN FOR ISURU UDANA).
TOSS - The flip of the coin has gone Aaron Finch's way and AUSTRALIA ELECT TO CHASE.

Time to talk about the action now. Erm... action... that is happening only from one side. The hosts have outplayed and outclassed the visitors and would like to end the first series of the cricketing summer with a thumping whitewash. David Warner has been the chief tormentor and is yet to be dismissed in the series. Australian skipper, Aaron Finch would hope that his side continues their brilliant form and make it 3-in-3. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, have a lot of work to do. They have not even threatened the hosts so far but would like to end their short tour with flying colours. It would be interesting to see how many changes they make in the side as they need to find a source of inspiration from somewhere. Can the Lankans put on a fight or will it be another stroll in the park for the Aussies? Welcome to the coverage of the final T20I game between Australia and Sri Lanka. Stay tuned to find out as the toss is not far away.

Before I welcome you to the coverage of the 3rd and final T20I between Australia and Sri Lanka, we would like to wish Maxwell all the power and strength and we hope to see him come back stronger than ever. Also, it takes a lot of strength to come out and speak about it openly so a special shout out for Maxwell to talk about his mental health issue openly. That has been the talk of the town as it is now time to think about players' well-being.
